title: Farmers protest police summons outside the Ministry of Internal Affairs
location: Outside the Ministry of Internal Affairs headquarters, Chișinău; exact gathering point not reported.
organizer: Unknown; sources identify a group of farmers but do not name an organizer for this Jan 25 action.
participants_original: TV8: “several farmers”; NewsMaker: “a group of farmers.” Neither report gives a number.
threshold_50_evidence: The opened contemporary sources describe “several” or a “group” of farmers but do not document 50 or more participants. The 50-person threshold remains pending.

title.summary: TV8 and NewsMaker describe a Jan 25 group of farmers protesting outside MAI after police citations tied to the prior December Parliament protest.

start_date.summary: TV8 dates the gathering 25 January at 11:39; NewsMaker also dates the gathering to 25 January; MAI refers to a protest organized “today” in its statement dated 25 January.

end_date.summary: Reports capture the gathering while underway and the request for a meeting but do not document participants leaving or the physical end. End date is unknown.

location.summary: TV8 and NewsMaker place the farmers outside MAI; the official MAI statement confirms the protest was at its headquarters.

scope.summary: The gathering took place at one ministry site in Chișinău; no multi-city organization is reported.

organizer.summary: Reports identify the participants as a group of farmers and their request for an audience, but do not name the organizer of the Jan 25 gathering. The names in the later MAI meeting refer to representatives of the broader 2020 farmer actions and are not assumed to be Jan 25 organizers.

demands.summary: Farmers sought explanations and an audience after police summons tied to the Dec 17 protest; a participant described the citations as intimidation. This supports the provisional police-brutality/arbitrary-action category as the protesters’ expressed grievance, not an independent finding that police acted unlawfully.

participants_original.summary: TV8 says “several farmers”; NewsMaker says a “group of farmers.”

participants_min.summary: No numeric minimum is reported; do not infer a count from “several” or “group.”

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The available contemporary reports do not establish 50 attendees; retain as pending_threshold.

protester_violence.summary: The January reports do not describe violence by participants in the Jan 25 action. Violence during the Dec 2020 Parliament action is a separate event and is not attributed here.

state_response.summary: NewsMaker dated Jan 25 reports that farmers obtained an audience with a state secretary that day; MAI separately confirms the interim minister met representatives on Feb 1 after their prior-week visit and petition. Both support accommodation, with the formal ministerial reception dated Feb 1. The Jan 25 reporting does not document arrests, beatings, dispersal, deliberate ignoring, killings or shootings. MAI’s broader allegations about violations, violence, road-blocking and case files concern the farmers’ 2020 mobilizations, not established conduct or arrests at this Jan 25 gathering.

eligibility.summary: The gathering directly sought a meeting with the domestic Interior Ministry over police sanctions; attendance remains unverified at 50 or more.

notes.summary: TV8 states the farm machinery was withdrawn from central Chișinău on Dec 30. The Jan 25 gathering concerns summons and sanctions after a Dec 17 action at Parliament, so it appears physically distinct; episode/campaign rules still require review.

open_questions.summary: Confirm whether this new gathering is a distinct episode under the original procedure, and whether independent contemporaneous evidence establishes the 50-person threshold and a physical end.

notes: A new gathering outside MAI on Jan 25 is reported after the farmers’ earlier Parliament protest. The immediate demand concerned police citations and an audience. NewsMaker reports a state-secretary audience on Jan 25; MAI separately confirms an interim-minister meeting on Feb 1 after the prior-week visit and petition. Neither date is used as the physical end of the Jan 25 gathering. TV8 says the earlier tractors were withdrawn Dec 30; do not attribute violence reported for the December action to this gathering. Review whether campaign/episode rules treat the Jan 25 action separately.
open_questions: What was the physical end time or date?
Does the original Coding Procedure treat the Jan 25 hearing protest as a new event or a phase of the December farmer campaign?
Was there any specific police action at the Jan 25 gathering beyond the state-secretary audience reported by NewsMaker?

title: Ocnița railway workers protest unpaid wages
location: Ocnița, Moldova; exact assembly site not reported.
organizer: Unknown; the sources do not identify a Jan 5 protest organizer.
participants_original: NewsMaker reports that railway workers in Ocnița protested over wages unpaid since October; no participant count is given. A Gagauzinfo search result also reports the protest but provides no count.
threshold_50_evidence: No numeric attendance estimate or clear qualitative wording establishing at least 50 is reported. The crowd threshold remains pending.

title.summary: NewsMaker reports that railway workers in Ocnița protested because they had not received wages; Gagauzinfo’s search result also identifies a Jan 5 protest there.

start_date.summary: NewsMaker’s Jan 22 explainer dates the Ocnița workers’ protest to Jan 5, 2021.

end_date.summary: The Jan 22 article reports the earlier Jan 5 protest but gives no end date or physical departure evidence.

location.summary: The report locates the protest in Ocnița; it does not specify a station, public square, or other exact gathering place.

scope.summary: The reported gathering involved workers at the Ocnița rail node; no other locations are linked to this specific Jan 5 action.

organizer.summary: A union federation chair is quoted discussing the broader CFM wage crisis, but neither source names an organizer for this Jan 5 local protest.

demands.summary: Workers said wages were unpaid since October. NewsMaker identifies CFM as a state enterprise and reports the union’s account of arrears and government assistance; this supports the provisional state-controlled labor/wage category.

participants_original.summary: NewsMaker says railway workers in Ocnița protested but provides no count; Gagauzinfo’s search result title gives no count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The sources establish a protest but do not establish a public gathering of at least 50 people.

protester_violence.summary: Neither source reports violence by participants in this Jan 5 action.

state_response.summary: The reviewed sources do not describe an action or inaction by the state in response to the Jan 5 Ocnița protest; all seven response values remain unknown.

eligibility.summary: The dispute concerns wage arrears at a state enterprise, but the 50-person threshold and exact public assembly context remain unverified.

notes.summary: NewsMaker distinguishes this Jan 5 Ocnița protest from a Dec 22 protest by workers in Basarabeasca. Do not merge the local actions solely because they concern CFM wages.

open_questions.summary: Check if the Jan 5 action was a public assembly, identify the exact site and any attendance estimate, and determine the physical end.

notes: CFM is described by NewsMaker as a state enterprise, supporting the state-controlled labor/wage rationale in the local codebook. The exact site, public-assembly form, organizer, attendance and end are not reported. A separate Dec 22 Basarabeasca wage protest is logged as a possible continuation; do not assume a nationally organized event or merge local actions without evidence.
open_questions: Did at least 50 workers or supporters assemble?
Was the action a public gathering or a workplace-only stoppage?
Who organized it and when did it physically end?
Does it form part of a larger coordinated CFM protest campaign?

title: Football supporters protest FMF leadership and seek investigation of match-fixing
location: Outside the Moldovan Football Federation in Chișinău; UNIMEDIA reports that participants later marched to the Presidential Administration and Prosecutor General, while NewsMaker places Rebeja and Democratic Party members at the Presidential Administration. Exact sequence and route require confirmation.
organizer: Radu Rebeja and his team; NewsMaker also reports Democratic Party members at the action.
participants_original: Știri.md / Infotag: headline says “about 50 people”; body says “over 50 supporters.” UNIMEDIA describes “several supporters” and gives no number.
threshold_50_evidence: The body of the Știri.md item says more than 50, but its headline says about 50. Given the boundary wording and lack of a second numeric count, the 50-person threshold remains pending.

title.summary: Local sports and news reports confirm a Jan 21 protest associated with Rebeja’s exclusion from the FMF presidential election.

start_date.summary: Moldfootball confirms the protest took place on Jan 21; UNIMEDIA also dates its report to Jan 21.

end_date.summary: The sources report the protest and a planned/later march but do not establish when participants dispersed.

location.summary: Moldfootball places the protest near FMF. UNIMEDIA reports a march to the Presidency and Prosecutor General; NewsMaker reports Rebeja and DPM members at the Presidential Administration.

scope.summary: The described stops are within Chișinău; no other city is linked to the Jan 21 action.

organizer.summary: Noi’s pre-event report attributes the call to Rebeja and his team; Moldfootball confirms the planned action occurred.

demands.summary: Sources report demands about Rebeja’s candidacy and voting in the FMF election. UNIMEDIA search text additionally says protesters asked the Prosecutor General to complete match-fixing investigations and hold responsible people accountable; use political_behavior_process provisionally because the state-directed demand is not independently opened and much of the dispute concerns private FMF governance.

participants_original.summary: Știri.md’s headline uses “about 50” while its body says “over 50”; UNIMEDIA uses only “several supporters.”

participants_min.summary: No stable numeric lower bound is used because “about 50” and “over 50” conflict at the eligibility boundary.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: One item reports “over 50” in the body but “about 50” in the headline; keep pending threshold pending a clearer or independent account.

protester_violence.summary: No reviewed source reports violence by participants at this gathering; the field remains unknown.

state_response.summary: No reviewed source documents accommodation, arrests, beatings, dispersal, ignoring, killings or shootings by Moldovan authorities in response to this gathering. Police supervision, where mentioned in a search result, is not itself a response code.

eligibility.summary: Most reporting focuses on an internal FMF election, a private sports federation. Only the UNIMEDIA search result reports a state-directed demand at the Prosecutor General; confirm that route and demand before state-target eligibility is resolved.

notes.summary: The Jan 21 protest concerns the FMF presidential election, not Moldova’s national election. It is not treated as a pro-state party rally. The private-federation grievance alone is not codeable; eligibility depends on the reported request to state prosecutors.

open_questions.summary: Confirm the government-directed demand and whether the FMF, Presidency and Prosecutor stops were one continuous gathering; reconcile attendance wording and assess political_behavior_process category.

notes: The immediate dispute concerns a private federation’s leadership election; sources describe the assembly as an FMF picket plus a reported march to state offices. Keep state-target eligibility pending because the prosecutorial demand and full route appear only in a search-only source. Attendance wording also straddles 50. This is not treated as a rally for state political office.
open_questions: Does an accessible source confirm the march to the Prosecutor General and a request for state action?
Were all reported sites part of one continuous public gathering?
Is political_behavior_process an appropriate category for the state-directed anti-match-fixing demand?
Did the state take any response beyond police presence?
